facts.statement: Protoalligator lived during the Paleocene epoch.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Paleocene

facts.statement: Protoalligator was found in the Wanghudun Formation of China.
facts.quote: Protoalligator is an extinct genus of alligatoroid from the Paleocene Wanghudun Formation of China.

facts.statement: The remains of Protoalligator huiningensis were first discovered in 1966 in Huaining County, Anhui Province, China.
facts.quote: The remains of Protoalligator huiningensis were first discovered in 1966 by a geological survey team in Huaining County of the Anhui Province, China

facts.statement: Protoalligator was first described as a species of Eoalligator by Yang Zhongjian in 1982.
facts.quote: They were subsequently described as a species of Eoalligator by Yang Zhongjian (also known as C.C. Young) in 1982

facts.statement: Protoalligator was placed in its own genus in 2016 by Wang, Sullivan, and Liu.
facts.quote: Wang, Sullivan and Liu addressed this issue by publishing a comprehensive revision of the three crocodilians in 2016

facts.statement: The proportions of the known specimen suggest Protoalligator had a relatively short snout.
facts.quote: with proportions suggesting that it was relatively short-snouted.

facts.statement: Protoalligator had an overbite, as all lower jaw teeth except the enlarged fourth one occluded medially to the upper jaw teeth.
facts.quote: With the exception of the enlarged fourth dentary tooth, all other teeth of the lower jaw would have occluded medially to those of the upper jaw, giving the animal an overbite.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Protoalligator belongs to the group Orientalosuchina and whether that group consists of alligatoroids.
facts.quote: Recent studies have suggested that Protoalligator was part of an early radiation of alligatoroids endemic to Asia known as orientalosuchins, though not all studies agree with it being placed within this group nor with orientalosuchins being alligatoroids in the first place.

facts.statement: Subsequent authors have continued to treat Protoalligator and Eoalligator as separate taxa despite their close relationship.
facts.quote: subsequent authors continued following Wang and colleagues in retaining them as two separate taxa distinguished in their anatomy.

facts.statement: The genus Protoalligator was named by Y. Wang, C. Sullivan, and J. Liu in 2016.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Y. Wang, C. Sullivan, & J. Liu, 2016

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Protoalligator is Protoalligator huiningensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Protoalligator huiningensis

facts.statement: Eoalligator huiningensis is a synonym of Protoalligator huiningensis.
facts.quote: synonyms: Eoalligator huiningensis C. Young, 1982

facts.statement: Protoalligator was an extinct crocodilian that lived in China during the Paleocene.
facts.quote: Protoalligator ("primer aligator") es un género extinto de crocodiliano, que vivió durante el Paleoceno en China.

facts.statement: The only known specimen, IVPP V4058, was found in the Wanghudun Formation in Anhui Province, China, dating to the middle Paleocene.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo y único conocido, IVPP V4058 fue descubierto en los depósitos de la Formación Wanghudun, en la provincia de Anhui en China, los cuales datan de mediados del Paleoceno.

facts.statement: The single known specimen consists of the anterior region of a mostly preserved right partial skull and the anterior part of the lower jaw, including some teeth still in their sockets.
facts.quote: El espécimen solo incluye la región anterior de un cráneo parcial mayormente conservado del lado derecho (con los huesos premaxilar, maxilar, nasal y parte de un yugal), junto con la parte anterior de la mandíbula (con partes de los huesos dentario, esplenial, angular, surangular y coracoides), además de algunos dientes aún en los alvéolos dentarios.

facts.statement: Unlike Asiatosuchus nanlingensis and many alligatoroids, the tip of the fourth lower tooth in Protoalligator is covered by a fossa located between the maxilla and premaxilla.
facts.quote: A diferencia de Asiatosuchus nanlingensis y muchos aligatoroideos, en Proalligator el ápice del cuarto diente inferior queda cubierto por una fosa situada entre el maxilar y el premaxilar

facts.statement: Protoalligator had a short snout with an anterior process on the premaxilla extending over the external naris, and its eleventh and twelfth lower teeth were the largest in the posterior mouth area, distinguishing it from modern alligators.
facts.quote: El hocico es corto y tiene un proceso anterior en el premaxilar que se extiende sobre la narina externa, los dientes inferiores undécimo y duodécimo son los mayores en tamaño en el área posterior de la boca, lo que lo distingue de los actuales aligatorinos.

facts.statement: A 2016 phylogenetic analysis suggests Protoalligator is a member of Alligatoroidea, indicated by its long surangular process.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético presentado por Wang et al., 2016, sugiere que Proalligator es miembro de Alligatoroidea, como indica su proceso surangular largo

facts.statement: It is debated whether Protoalligator belongs to the clade Orientalosuchina, as some studies exclude it from the group.
facts.quote: However, even disregarding studies published prior to the naming of the clade, not all studies find Protoalligator as a member of Orientalosuchina.

facts.statement: Protoalligator lived between 66 and 61.66 million years ago during the Danian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Danian to Danian (66 to 61.66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The name Protoalligator was coined in 2016 by Y. Wang, C. Sullivan, and J. Liu specifically for E. huiningensis after E. chunyii was synonymized with Asiatosuchus nanlingensis.
facts.quote: La especie tipo de Eoalligator, E. chunyii, es un sinónimo más moderno de Asiatosuchus nanlingensis, de modo que en 2016 fue acuñado el nuevo nombre de género Protoalligator específicamente para "E." huiningensis por Y. Wang, C. Sullivan, y J. Liu.
